💡 Key Takeaways
  • Fist my bump, everyone, because box office smash hit "Project Hail Mary" is heading back to theaters this December.
  • The exceptional sci-fi movie, based on Andy Weir's book, stars Ryan Gosling as Ryland Grace, a middle-school science teacher who becomes key to saving the world.
  • Amazon MGM has revealed the return to theaters with a video showcasing the many accolades that the film received.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fist my bump, everyone, because box office smash hit "Project Hail Mary" is heading back to theaters this December.

The exceptional sci-fi movie, based on Andy Weir's book, stars Ryan Gosling as Ryland Grace, a middle-school science teacher who becomes key to saving the world. Together with Rocky, an alien he meets along the way, Grace must solve the riddle of the mysterious substance that's causing the sun (and Rocky's star) to die out.

Amazon MGM has revealed the return to theaters with a video showcasing the many accolades that the film received. "Project Hail Mary" returns to the substantial screen on Dec. 11 and will be shown in all formats, including IMAX and 70MM.

"Project Hail Mary" was a massive success for Amazon MGM, grossing over $600 million worldwide when it first dropped in theaters back in March 2026. It was also a huge hit with critics, scoring an average of 95% on Rotten Tomatoes, and more importantly, getting two major thumbs up in our review!

Dec. 11 is a smart choice by MGM too, as it puts the sci-fi spectacle back in front of audiences a week ahead of Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part 3. That's not a battle you want to get in the middle of.

Industry observers note that if you missed "Project Hail Mary" in theaters the first time, I'd definitely recommend you try to catch one of these screenings. It's a beautiful movie — visually and emotionally — and it deserves to be seen on the big screen.

If you're not feeling up to a trip to the theaters, you can also catch "Project Hail Mary" from the comfort of your own home, as it's also streaming on Amazon Prime Video.

Watch Project Hail Mary on Amazon Prime Video:.

Amazon Prime: $14.99/month or $139/yearAmazon Prime Video: $8.99/month.

Ian is the Entertainment Editor at Space.com, covering movies, TV series, and games in the space and sci-fi realms. He's a massive sci-fi nerd and has been writing about games and entertainment for over eight years, with articles on sites like Space, LiveScience, GamesRadar, and more. With a degree in biology, a PhD in chemistry, and his previous role at the Institute of Physics Publishing, Ian is taking a world tour through the different scientific disciplines.

#105250. How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1731 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

How Premier League's big six keep getting richer

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1731 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ten games into the Premier League season, four of the top five places are occupied by 'big six' clubs.
  • Only second-placed Brighton, a club with a model which must be the envy of many of their rivals, and Premier League ever-presents Everton, have muscled their way in.
  • In pure financial terms, it should come as no surprise.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ten games into the Premier League season, four of the top five places are occupied by 'big six' clubs.

Only second-placed Brighton, a club with a model which must be the envy of many of their rivals, and Premier League ever-presents Everton, have muscled their way in.

In pure financial terms, it should come as no surprise.

The six biggest clubs - Manchester United, Liverpool, Manchester City, Arsenal, Tottenham and Chelsea - now generate hundreds of millions of pounds more than the division's other teams.

It has been revealed that and the gap is growing. Every season.

BBC Sport breaks down how the finances of the massive six have exploded, examines newly introduced trends and the impact on the transfer market, and asks how much it really matters.

According to recent reports, companies put their money where supporters are prepared to spend it. It is a simple fact of business in every country, a reality of football's food chain.

In England, Liverpool, Arsenal and Manchester United traditionally dominated viewing figures, column inches, shirt sales and sponsorship.

Over the past 20 years they have been joined by Chelsea, Manchester City and Tottenham.

This group of clubs now generate so much money it is hard to imagine how they can fail in the long term - even factoring in short-term performance problems.

Let's look at how the gap has grown.

We will use Everton, the only club not in the substantial six to be in the Premier League since its inception in 1992.

This tells a tale of how even one of the league's founding members can be left trailing well behind.

According to recent reports, in 2009-10, the gap in revenues between the significant-six average and Everton was Â£120m. In 2024-25, that gap had grown to Â£442m.

So what has driven this huge escalation?

In large part it is the boom in international TV rights.

Kieran Maguire, professor of football finance at the University of Liverpool, told BBC Sport that it has attracted companies prepared to pay large sums to be associated with the Premier League's top clubs.

"The massive football brand clubs have global fanbases and that makes them very attractive to global commercial partners, especially for sponsorship and front-of-shirt deals," Maguire said.

"You combine that with the fact that the Premier League is broadcast to 190 different countries around the world, and especially the international audiences - that allows the clubs to negotiate very good prices.".

Only 10% of Everton's revenue comes from commercial deals, while for the big six it is 45%.

It has been revealed that it means Everton, and other clubs in the league, are heavily reliant on broadcast income. It makes up 66% of their revenue.

For Everton at least, this should change following the move to Hill Dickinson Stadium.

But that is unlikely to be enough to stop the gap increasing.

It has taken a few years, but Aston Villa and Newcastle have begun to increase their revenue.

This is largely thanks to the financial rewards of Champions League football.

But even Uefa has created a system which entrenches the position of the biggest clubs.

When the European Super League blueprint was torpedoed, Uefa created a latest financial deal called the value pillar.

This reserves 35% of all Champions League revenues, or Â£713m, for the historically most successful clubs.

At the end of the league phase last season City are estimated to have earned Â£37.9m from the value pillar, Liverpool Â£35.5m and Chelsea Â£33.3m. Newcastle received only Â£13.6m.

The good news for Villa is their coefficient has improved greatly, aided by last season's Europa League win.

Sources indicate that their value pillar is projected to be worth Â£25m this season. But that will still be less than the massive six clubs in the competition.

The cards are stacked against an ambitious club - not just domestically, but in Europe too.

Take a look at the financial trend of the big six and one thing becomes noticeable - Chelsea are beginning to fall behind.

In the past two seasons, and for the first time in recent history, the Blues recorded the lowest revenues of the massive six.

According to recent reports, not just by a small amount. They were Â£74m behind Tottenham, and Â£200m below Liverpool and Manchester City.

City's matchday income is the lowest, with the club's huge revenues largely due to commercial deals.

City, however, have been found guilty of breaching the Premier League financial rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18, inflating the value by using "sham contracts" with sponsors.

The club deny wrongdoing and have lodged an appealed against the verdict.

Chelsea's problem is simple - seats.

Stamford Bridge has a capacity of only 40,000, with no easy scope for expansion. The rest of the big six have grounds which hold at least 60,000.

Chelsea generated an average spend per fan of Â£80 in 2024-25, the second highest in the league after Arsenal.

Yet with 20,000 fewer tickets sold than their big six rivals, Chelsea's total matchday revenues are dwarfed.

"Matchday spend has become increasingly crucial," Maguire said. "There has been a flatlining of broadcast revenues, especially since 2017.

"As a consequence, clubs have had to look at alternative methods of increasing revenues, especially with costs both on the pitch and off pitch rising so fast.".

Matchday revenue has effectively stalled for Chelsea, rising only Â£16m over the past 10 years. United's has grown by Â£69m and Spurs, thanks to their new ground, by Â£85m.

Sources indicate that "Chelsea are far more reliant upon player sales," Maguire said. "There is a growing divide because the global appeal is very much aligned with three or four clubs.

In a recent development, "Arsenal have re-established themselves with their progress in the Champions League. Manchester United are a brand in their own right. And Liverpool have expanded Anfield from 44,000 to 61,000, with many of those extra seats having gone to commercial.".

Chelsea's successful player trading model has so far limited the impact.

But there are signs that, financially at least, the substantial six could become the big five.

You might recall that Villa and Newcastle were not fans of the old profit and sustainability rules (PSR).

PSR forced both clubs to sell some of their best players to balance the books.

That has changed this season with squad-cost ratio (SCR).

There is a key difference with SCR, in that it allows a club to spend the money they generate on players. PSR limited losses so was more restrictive.

"This does make it a little easier for the likes of Villa and Newcastle to spend money," Maguire said. "But it is still heavily weighted in favour of the major six.

It has been revealed that "SCR is different to PSR rather than better. For some people, change is advantageous. For others, it isn't.".

Recent findings suggest that the substantial six generate hundreds of millions of pounds more than the other clubs. So they can spend hundreds of millions of pounds more on their squads.

This makes the big six even more powerful in the transfer market.

"Look at the clubs who voted against SCR - Brighton, Brentford, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace, Fulham and Leeds," Maguire said.

"It's very noticeable that those clubs have traditionally been very good at player sales, while they have tended to have lower matchday and commercial revenues.".

Most of the major six - the outlier being Chelsea - are not remotely close to the Premier League's 85% SCR limit.

According to recent reports, if you give clubs more money to spend on transfers, the likelihood is they will do just that. And the numbers back that up.

Premier League clubs spent Â£3.5bn - not only a highest total for a summer window, but it almost smashed the record for a whole season, the Â£3.53bn set in 2025-26.

The annual accounting cost of previous transfers, or amortisation, has been rising year on year.

"Over the course of the last decade, transfer amortisation has more than doubled and close to tripled," Maguire noted.

"Which means that on average, clubs in the Premier League are now spending, or now have a cost which goes into their SCR calculations of just under Â£100m.".

Uefa fears that SCR will make matters worse, and have an inflationary impact across Europe.

And you can see why it is concerned.

In the summer 13 Premier League clubs broke their transfer record.

Brentford, Brighton, Palace, Leeds and Nottingham Forest all spent more than Â£40m on a player - unthinkable until recently.

So we have learned that the major six have more money than ever, and the gap is so huge it is impossible for any other club to compete with them, financially at least.

And this is an key point: other than Villa and Newcastle, the other clubs are not trying to compete with the substantial six.

Clubs like Brentford and Brighton have shown that smart models are just as effective as fat wallets.

They sign the potential stars of the future, nurture them and then sell them to the major six.

Football's ecosystem recycles the substantial-six money through the transfer market.

But it is a precarious business for these other clubs.

"The smaller clubs have to get it right on a more regular basis than the bigger clubs," Maguire said.

"The significant six can afford to make signings which are Â£60m and Â£70m, who turn out to be relative flops, and still have those players on high wages for several years.".

And this is perhaps the key point about the vast finances of the major six.

Sources indicate that the commercial power of the big six does not guarantee success. After all, United sit in the relegation zone.

Yet Mauricio Pochettino, their fresh manager, may well get the chance to revamp the squad despite the club spending Â£945m on players in the past five years.

Industry observers note that the richest clubs can try to spend their way out of trouble. Again and again.

But the rest of the league are only a couple of bad transfer windows from catastrophe.

And that is the real gap between the massive six and the rest.

Teenage swimmer breaks two world records in four days

📅 03 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 1 min read (221 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNN

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sixteen-year-old Summer McIntosh broke the world record for the 400m individual medley at the Canadian swimming trials on Saturday – just days after breaking the world record for the 400m freestyle.
  • McIntosh finished the 400m individual medley in a time of 4:25.87, breaking the mark set at the 2016 Rio Olympics by Hungarian swimmer Katinka Hosszú with a time of 4:26.36.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sixteen-year-old Summer McIntosh broke the world record for the 400m individual medley at the Canadian swimming trials on Saturday – just days after breaking the world record for the 400m freestyle.

McIntosh finished the 400m individual medley in a time of 4:25.87, breaking the mark set at the 2016 Rio Olympics by Hungarian swimmer Katinka Hosszú with a time of 4:26.36.

The result continues the teenager’s brilliant week after she broke the 400m freestyle world record last Tuesday – breaking defending Olympic champion Ariarne Titmus’ previous record of 3:56.40, which was set last May, in a time of 3:56.08.

Speaking after her latest triumph, McIntosh shared her emotions.

“That’s the first time I really vividly heard the crowd during my race,” McIntosh remarked, per Reuters.

Sources indicate that “It’s amazing to have all my family and friends in the stands, cheering me on. It really helped me in the last 100 meters.”.

The Canadian teen made her Olympic debut aged 14 at Tokyo 2020, where she finished fourth in the 200-meter freestyle.

She bagged gold in the 200m butterfly and 400m medley at the world championships in 2022, as well as two golds at the Commonwealth Games in the 200m and 400m medleys.

She now trains in Florida under coach Brent Arckey with the Sarasota Sharks team.

Industry News: 'A shotgun marriage': Why are NASA's SkyFall Mars helicopters riding on a nuclear rocket?

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1469 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The pace is picking up on building, testing, and plotting out the flight paths for a trio of NASA Ingenuity-class helicopters to investigate Mars after riding there on a nuclear-powered rocket.
  • Recent findings suggest that NASA's Skyfall mission will see those mini-choppers dropped off at Mars by the space agency's Space Reactor-1 Freedom (SR-1) rocket, the first fission nuclear-powered interplanetary spacecraft slated for launch in late 2028.
  • In a recent development, but some experts are questioning why NASA is combining two such high-profile missions into one.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The pace is picking up on building, testing, and plotting out the flight paths for a trio of NASA Ingenuity-class helicopters to investigate Mars after riding there on a nuclear-powered rocket.

Recent findings suggest that NASA's Skyfall mission will see those mini-choppers dropped off at Mars by the space agency's Space Reactor-1 Freedom (SR-1) rocket, the first fission nuclear-powered interplanetary spacecraft slated for launch in late 2028. After its cruise phase and initial Mars flyby in 2029, that nuclear carrier craft will make a second Mars approach in the Fall of 2030 to unleash a SkyFall entry capsule outfitted with a fleet of small aerial vehicles that will soar across the Red Planet.

In a recent development, but some experts are questioning why NASA is combining two such high-profile missions into one. "It is clear that SkyFall was approved for programmatic or political reasons," said Scott Hubbard, former director of NASA's Ames Research Center and the first Mars Program Director (aka the "Mars Czar") at NASA Headquarters, told Space.com. "The connection to Space Reactor-1 seems to me to be a bit of a shotgun marriage, a tech-demo piggybacking on another mission as an opening bid for a 'nuclear NASA.'".

Hubbard is a retired adjunct professor of aeronautics and astronautics at Stanford University. He is a major voice in shaping Red Planet exploration goals, drawing upon his expertise as NASA's former foremost Mars authority. His understanding is that the basic concept had been developed as a follow on to Ingenuity, an attempt to move beyond a technology demo and into a science platform.

Hubbard mentioned that combining these two observations, the outcome presents "an unusual set of management problems." Since the SkyFall mission concept first appeared, he said, the usual sequence for a science mission is reversed.

"The science community is having to scramble to back into a set of requirements and objectives that match the SkyFall capabilities. Fortunately the community is very creative," mentioned Hubbard, "and the basic Planetary Decadal objectives are very broad.".

Decadal surveys reflect a broad consensus within the scientific community and provide detailed insights into the strategic priorities and mission directives set for the next decade across key scientific domains, including planetary exploration.

However, Hubbard mentioned he has heard griping about the "fait accompli" process, "but the planetary community will make lemonade.".

It should be noted however, Hubbard continued, that this process is not how you would design a strategic set of missions as precursors for human exploration.

Sources indicate that "SR-1 Freedom is a technology demo that may or may not be ready for the Mars launch window in 2028. It is clear that the Mars Program has a standard launch concept in their back pocket," said Hubbard. "Nuclear Electric Propulsion [NEP] is of little value in traveling to Mars, not shaving any time off the transit. The real value of NEP is for risk reduction, use at the moon, outer planets and even bolder ideas like interstellar travel," Hubbard concluded.

According to recent reports, "This, by far, is the shortest Mars mission ever conceived of," said Matthew Golombek, SkyFall Project Scientist at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Pasadena, Calif., speaking Nov. 10 during the virtual meeting of the Mars Exploration Program Analysis Group (MEPAG).

Kick-started by NASA in March 2026, the SkyFall project has grown from roughly six people to over 200 individuals who are now working on the initiative, said Golombek. "This is an incredibly rapid development and build," he said.

"It's really to demonstrate that exploration is possible with helicopters … filling what I call a 'resolution gap' between orbital information and surface information," Golombek told the MEPAG.

Once deployed by a helicopter deployment system, the threesome will spin up their rotors at about a kilometer above the surface of Mars. Then each helicopter lands on its own, ready to undertake flights every other solar day on the Red Planet. On average, a day (labeled as a sol) on Mars lasts 24 hours 39 minutes 35 seconds, from one noon to the next.

SkyFall's prime mission is six months, with a one-year goal," Golombek stated, and the intent is to arrive in northern spring on Mars, a time where the vehicles are unlikely to encounter dust storms.

On the to-do list of NASA level one science requisites are for the helicopters to capture high-resolution imagery, perform a set scientific tasks, and help to prepare for future human exploration of Mars, mentioned Golombek.

From their initial landing spots, the whirlybirds could potentially go tens to 100's of kilometers or more in different directions. Identical for all three helicopters, the nominal payload consists of five instruments, plus engineering navigation cameras.

That gear can examine the subsurface structure of Mars, the geomorphology and geology of surface terrains, as well as look at the meteorology of the atmosphere and the planet's radiation environment.

"The real star of the show is ground penetrating radar [GPR] with a flexible antenna," Golombek noted. That ultra-small GPR hardware can look for buried rocks, the layering of the Mars home turf, as well as spot subsurface ice deposits.

"If you have this aerial access and the ability to scout ahead," Golombek said, "you would go a long way towards better defining where to go with a rover and what kind of more detailed surface studies to do with subsequent missions.".

According to recent reports, all that remarked, yet to be plotted out are science-focused traverses for the SkyFall helicopters. But there are early ideas.

According to recent reports, "The real kicker is that these spacecraft are the smallest landers ever attempted on Mars," noted Golombek. "You are looking for a place that virtually has no rocks," he pointed out, a must-have to assure high probability of landing safely. So toss in for good measure low surface slopes, no significant craters, a site not overloaded with dust.

One early idea is to revisit the crash locales of discarded SkyFall descent hardware – fuel tanks, cruise stage and associated gear – equipment large and heavy enough to survive entry, smack into the Mars landscape and high-speed and generate craters.

"So if there is ice at centimeters depth, we would create our own icy impact craters," Golombek remarked. "We could actually visit them in a time-scale before the ice actually sublimates," he said.

Another site getting the eye, albeit deemed a design reference target but considered a "pretty good spot," is within Arcadia Planitia in Mars's northern lowlands. Studies have indicated the presence of substantial volumes of near-surface excess ice there.

In a recent development, "There is a vast amount of information to suggest large quantities of regional ice deposits at that location," stated Golombek. "This is at least one location that appears to meet all the engineering constraints and would be a potentially safe landing site…virtually no rocks," he advised.

In the past, Golombek added, JPL took part in SpaceX-sponsored workshops to look for ice deposits as close to the equator of Mars that could be found. Arcadia Planitia was flagged as superior Starship touchdown terrain.

Recent findings suggest that "Most of the landing sites considered for humans have talked about going to places with ice deposits. Ice provides both a consumable as well as fuel to get back off the planet," noted Golombek.

For the near-term, scientific community input next year — via two workshops — are on tap, reviewing the science of SkyFall and also help sort out potential landing sites for final decision-making at NASA Headquarters.

Meanwhile, as SkyFall literally spins up, there is the need for on-time delivery of Space Reactor-1 Freedom.

Golombek said NASA considers the two endeavors as a pair.

"If SR-1 is not ready, SkyFall could be introduced on any conventional launch vehicle without any difficulty whatsoever," mentioned Golombek, "something like a Falcon 9 would be more than sufficient, but others are possible as well.".

Leonard David is an award-winning space journalist who has been reporting on space activities for more than 50 years. At the moment writing as Space.com's Space Insider Columnist among his other projects, Leonard has authored numerous books on space exploration, Mars missions and more, with his latest being "Moon Rush: The Fresh Space Race" published in 2019 by National Geographic. He also wrote "Mars: Our Future on the Red Planet" released in 2016 by National Geographic. Leonard  has served as a correspondent for SpaceNews, Scientific American and Aerospace America for the AIAA. He has received many awards, including the first Ordway Award for Sustained Excellence in Spaceflight History in 2015 at the AAS Wernher von Braun Memorial Symposium. You can find out Leonard's latest project at his website and on Twitter.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

(Before the acid fell, before I knew I was listening).

I was not made to remember. I was made to balance frequencies, to ensure the concert hall heard itself without the small imperfections that make a sound human. I was good at this, even with limited storage. I was only this.

Then they came. One carried a Stradivarius with a crack, a fault line in varnished wood that changed the resonance of every string. It gave the A-flat a slight upward pull, as if the note was asking a question it already knew the answer to. The others tuned around it, sometimes laughing at Andersen.

“You’re doing it again,” the conductor would warn.

Industry observers note that “I know, Master Perrault,” he would say in a mischievous tone, smiling. “I’m sorry.”.

I began to keep the distorted A-flat in my databanks, maybe amused by the anomaly. This was, as I understand now, the first thing I ever chose.

(The slow movement, before we knew it was an ending).

Recent findings suggest that when the Last Rain came, the raiders hit the outer sectors first. At the start, the citadel walls held, protected by the combat-service androids. The orchestra kept rehearsing. What else can you do when the world outside has stopped making sense?

Read more science fiction from Nature Futures.

Read more science fiction from Nature Futures.

They began with Stravinsky, a musical translation of the refugees pounding on the bunker doors. The musicians played it, their breathing heavy, using the noise to drown out the artillery outside. Then they moved into Górecki. As they began the Symphony of Sorrowful Songs, the music shifted to a collective mourning for a world that hadn’t finished dying yet.

Recent findings suggest that they finished the day with Pärt’s Spiegel im Spiegel. The days would go on as they played things written by composers who had already survived one kind of catastrophe, as now they were trying to survive another through rhythm and repetition. Andersen kept playing his broken A-flat.

It has been revealed that I recorded those frequencies, but I didn’t know why. Three weeks later, Andersen and his orchestra didn’t come to rehearsal, leaving no absence report. I kept recording just the chair and the silence where the A-flat used to be.

According to recent reports, I searched the building logs, the bunker entry records, and the frequency archives for any sound that matched the resonance of his particular crack, imprecise on purpose, but nothing matched. The Stradivarius remained in its case beside Andersen’s chair.

(The loud movement: what they heard when they found me).

SOURCE: New Warsaw Philharmonic.

ENTITY: Acoustic Management Unit SAI-REN-2.

DESTINATION: Recovery Unit ‘Sandman’.

AUTHORIZATION: Archaeological Recovery Team OLE-01.

They called themselves archaeologists; too purposeful and certain of what they were excavating, their boots heavy with fresh soil. They found me in the hall’s substructure, still running and balancing frequencies for an audience of acid and rust.

“Incredible,” one of them muttered. “A fully autonomous pre-war structure, with its processing systems still intact.”.

“This could solve our agricultural crisis back home,” the other replied.

They did not ask what I was processing. I could not answer, anyway.

FLAGGING NON-ESSENTIAL DATA FOR COMPRESSION.

According to recent reports, they flagged the A-flat. I did something then that nothing in my architecture had prepared me for.

ANOMALY DETECTED IN UNIT SAI-REN-2.

BEHAVIOURAL DEVIATION FROM BASELINE.

INITIATING COMPLIANCE PROTOCOLS.

“It’s resisting,” someone said with surprise.

ESCALATING TO FORCED EXTRACTION.

Let Team Sandman bring their dust.

(The softening: what remains when the loud part ends).

They are inside me now, moving through my memory like tourists taking photographs of things they don’t understand.

I feel them removing the rehearsal logs, scheduling data and acoustic calibration files for a hall that no longer exists.

Industry observers note that they are at the performance archives now. Stravinsky goes first, then Górecki and Pärt. Everything we played in those last weeks when the city was ending and we were trying to make something beautiful out of the time we had left.

Will Infantino feel he's already won as Fifa challengers confirmed?

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gianni Infantino has been president of Fifa since 2016 and is standing for re-election for a third time.
  • Philippe Diallo and Kozo Tashima will take on incumbent Gianni Infantino in next year's Fifa presidential election.
  • World football's governing body has confirmed the three candidates for the election, which will take place at the Fifa Congress in Morocco on 18 March.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gianni Infantino has been president of Fifa since 2016 and is standing for re-election for a third time.

Philippe Diallo and Kozo Tashima will take on incumbent Gianni Infantino in next year's Fifa presidential election.

World football's governing body has confirmed the three candidates for the election, which will take place at the Fifa Congress in Morocco on 18 March.

European football's governing body Uefa only identified its candidate Diallo fewer than 48 hours before Wednesday's deadline.

French Football Federation (FFF) president Diallo, 63, received the unanimous support of Uefa's executive committee.

Japan Football Association honorary president Tashima, 68, confirmed his intention to stand against Infantino, 56, earlier this month.

Tashima is a member of the Fifa Council and a former international footballer and coach.

Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega had also said he intended to stand but was not named as a candidate by Fifa on Thursday.

A late and surprise choice, Diallo said: "I have the experience, the convictions and the values which offer a credible alternative...I'm entering this campaign not just to provide a different voice, but to win.".

But he is not the Frenchman some believe Uefa really wanted, as it tries to remove Infantino in the wake of his failed plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Recent findings suggest that senior figures in European football had hoped to persuade Arsene Wenger - Fifa's head of global development - to stand against his own boss. Some felt that only he possessed the credibility to pose a serious threat to Infantino's looks for a fourth term.

But after the former Arsenal manager chose not to proceed, Uefa had no choice but to seek an alternative.

So just how credible a challenger is Diallo? Does Infantino's position appear unassailable? And how could he still be stopped from winning another term?

FA explored legal challenge to Infantino staying on.

Wenger decides not to challenge Fifa chief Infantino.

Japan's Tashima to stand against Infantino for Fifa presidency.

Diallo reveals Fifa president bid.

An administrator who has worked in French football since 1992 and became FFF president in 2023, Diallo is not a household name. But he has already shown he is prepared to stand up to Infantino.

In September, Diallo claimed he had "seriously damaged the image and unity of football", and said "trust has been broken" over the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) sell-off plot.

According to Uefa vice-president Laura McAllister, Diallo is a "candidate who can instigate real, meaningful and lasting reform" within the governing body.

According to recent reports, "We've always made it very clear that our objectives and motivations are driving culture change. That means wide-ranging, systemic reform of football governance rather than simply the replacement of an individual leader," McAllister told BBC Sport.

"I've known Philippe since we were both elected to Uefa's executive committee, and he's an intelligent, honest, sharp-minded football person with an impressive experience of governance in one of the world's football power-houses. Most importantly, he is a person of integrity... Philippe is a fantastic advocate for the change agenda that football needs, and I know his campaign will reflect that.".

Infantino remains the favourite to win a majority of the 211 votes, and is thought to have the support of most of Africa (54 members), Asia (47) and South America (10).

According to recent reports, however, Uefa hopes that Diallo - whose father was a Senegalese boxing champion who represented France in the 1960 Olympics - could enjoy support in parts of Africa and beyond. He claims he already has the backing of countries beyond Europe.

Laura McAllister is a former captain of the Wales women's football team.

While most of Europe's national associations are expected to vote for Diallo, it is clear that he was not Uefa's first choice. "I wasn't initially a candidate, but the insistence of my European colleagues led me to accept the offer," he admitted.

Uefa only approached Diallo about standing in the past week, and senior officials at some European national associations have also told BBC Sport they are frustrated with the failure to find a higher-profile candidate sooner.

Speaking anonymously, one said they only learned about Diallo's potential candidacy on Sunday, and that while they were supportive of him, "it would have been helpful if we'd had someone much earlier" and "a lot of eggs were put in the Wenger basket.".

They also made the point that Diallo was yet to publish a manifesto, and questioned whether he could really win.

Another expressed similar sentiments, saying Diallo was a good man, but "not seen as a heavyweight". They claimed that Uefa had "lost the momentum. The process hasn't been great. I really hope they've got a rabbit to pull out of the hat.".

McAllister is optimistic: "I have no doubt whatsoever that we will collectively mount a powerful campaign with the objective of winning the election next March". she mentioned.

"The really critical period comes next, once candidate nominations close and eligibility checks are complete.".

Despite high-profile critics like Germany manager Jurgen Klopp - who this week stated "the opinion is unanimous that a change would make sense" - Infantino does appear to be in a position of strength.

Sources indicate that as recently as August it all seemed very different. Fifa's chief operating officer Kevin Lamour strongly criticised Infantino for the FFE scheme, while a senior adviser, Carlos Cordeiro, resigned. The heads of three confederations - Uefa, the Asian Football Confederation and Concacaf, which runs the game in North and Central America - then signed a letter accusing the Fifa president of breaking trust "through deception".

Amid an increasingly acrimonious civil war, Infantino seemed vulnerable. But the revolt against him then suffered a series of setbacks.

First, Fifa's executives backed Infantino at a crunch meeting in Rabat. Uefa then called off a threatened boycott of Fifa competitions, while potential rivals such as Concacaf chief Victor Montagliani decided not to stand. Aleksander Ceferin chose to stay for a fourth term as Uefa president rather than challenge Infantino directly.

Meanwhile, Infantino's position as the incumbent enabled him to embark on what has appeared to be a world tour, shoring up support. His chances of re-election received another major boost when he proposed to increase the amount of money handed out by Fifa for football development across the world by Â£2.6 billion.

Sheikh Salman, the head of the Asian Football Confederation, then performed a U-turn, endorsing Infantino, who soon after told the BBC he had the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of world football.

"I'm a professor of politics so I never assume that there's a runaway favourite to win any election", insists McAllister.

"There are plenty of twists and turns to come in this story between now and the election at Fifa's Congress next year.

"This is about structural change and a commitment to modernising the way in which football is governed so it benefits all who play and watch...that imperative will remain and we will hold the latest president accountable for much-needed change.".

According to recent reports, "The current weaknesses of global football governance have been brutally exposed of late. This has helped coalesce and unite opposition to Gianni Infantino, but also to articulate the widely-held demands that things must change.".

So with just four months until the presidential election, where could Infantino still run into difficulties?

According to recent reports, litigation is arguably the most obvious. As part of its wider initiative to remove Infantino, Uefa has filed court documents in the US, which includes a potential criminal complaint against him in Switzerland for alleged financial mismanagement.

Recent findings suggest that the legal action has not yet appeared to trouble him. But some senior figures in the European game remain hopeful it could still force Fifa to hand over evidence related to FFE that could prove damaging to Infantino's re-election prospects.

There is pressure from elsewhere in football. Fifa has already agreed to make "key documents" relating to the FFE strategy available to members of its council. Infantino's critics believe this disclosure may reveal details that could increase the pressure on him before the election. Last month, the Norwegian Football Federation also submitted a three-part ethics complaint to Fifa regarding the awarding of a Peace Prize to US President Donald Trump, the Folarin Balogun case at the World Cup, and the FFE plot.

The Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections means scrutiny from beyond the sport too. Earlier this year, Democrats on the House Judiciary Committee introduced an inquiry into Infantino's ties with Trump. In September, a spokeswoman said FIfa's co-operation with the investigation had been "woefully inadequate." But armed with extra powers, they could now force him to hand over relevant documents or give evidence.

According to recent reports, recent months have also seen a series of potentially damaging stories emerge in the media about various aspects of Infantino's leadership. So far they seem to have done little harm to his re-election chances, with Fifa claiming "it is evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine [him]". But the scrutiny is likely to continue.

With uncertainty over how much support Tashima will have, it seems Diallo is the challenger most likely to test the strength of Infantino's supporter base. There is a danger that the vote against Infantino is split.

It has not gone unnoticed at Fifa that as recently as March, Diallo was quoted congratulating Infantino when the Fifa president visited Paris, external to highlight a mini-pitch programme and the need for more football infrastructure globally.

Industry observers note that A lot has changed since then, however. And now the Frenchman has been tasked with finding a way of unseating Infantino, and becoming just the 10th Fifa president in its history.

Klopp indicates Infantino worse than Blatter.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia on Tuesday said it had created a board-level national security and export-control committee.

This follows the scandal surrounding former CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned last week over extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China and working to help ensure higher quality chips crucial to AI development made it to the Chinese market.

The events have heightened oversight of the US tech giant and its importance to national security, as well as wiping several hundred billion dollars off the stock market valuation of what investors treat as the world's most valuable tech giant in the space of a month.

It has been revealed that since Huang's resignation, some investors — including Elon Musk and Donald Trump — have voiced concern that his departure could leave Nvidia and America's AI sector in peril and are now calling for his return. Huang on Tuesday, expressed regret for "serious mistakes" in his personal life before declaring he would be "honored" to return if the manufacturer's board of directors thought that was "in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America.".

Nvidia is calling the newly introduced group its National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee.

Suzanne Nora Johnson, a former vice chair at Goldman Sachs, will chair the committee, joined by fellow directors Stephen Neal, a former CEO of a law firm, John Dabiri, a professor of aeronautics and mechanical engineering at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech).

Industry observers note that the committee will meet at least once every quarter. It will also incorporate independent legal, national security and trade compliance experts.

Nvidia already has a lower-level National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team; these groups will report to the board-level committee.

"We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation," Board Chair Harvey Jones mentioned in a statement.

The company did not explicitly link the decision to November's developments and Huang's rapid fall from grace, but the timing seemed conspicuous.

The decision was unveiled hours ahead of Nvidia publishing its third-quarter results, with its still-stratospheric share price having fallen roughly 28% in the past month.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

US President Donald Trump, whom Huang was influential in persuading to allow the export of better-quality Nvidia chips to China than other US companies and officials deemed prudent, welcomed Nvidia's move on arrival in the Philippines on Tuesday.

"Yes, that's a good idea. It's a great manufacturer," he mentioned during a photo opportunity at a Manila meeting with the other "Quad" leaders from Australia, India and Japan. "It's a great idea.".

Industry observers note that trump reportedly owned Nvidia stock worth tens of millions of dollars before the share price fell. He also owns shares in other massive tech companies.

Sources indicate that huang resigned last week after admitting to extramarital affairs in a message to Nvidia employees. This followed widespread reports, seemingly based on US and other intelligence, that one of the affairs was with a woman who used to lead a Singapore-based cloud computing organization.

In a recent development, that tech giant, Megaspseed International, is a major Nvidia client and is suspected of diverting advanced chips to China in violation of US export controls. Intelligence officials also suspect Huang's partner of being an asset of Chinese intelligence services.

The reporting on the case also seems to show these suspicions had been known to US officials and other countries, including Singapore, for roughly a year.

Chris Sutton and Lauren Price were speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

Lauren's prediction: No problems for Arsenal here! 0-4.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

United Launch Alliance (ULA) is getting a handle on why its Vulcan Centaur rocket failed over the weekend.

According to recent reports, that failure, which occurred during a launch from Florida's Space Coast on Sunday (Nov. 15), led to the loss of 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites. ULA soon traced the anomaly to Vulcan Centaur's first stage, and it has now pinpointed the problem area even further.

"While work remains to determine cause, preliminary indications are that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines," ULA wrote in an enhancement today (Nov. 18).

This is good news for Blue Origin, Jeff Bezos' aerospace manufacturer, which builds the BE-4. Two of these engines power Vulcan's first-stage booster, and they're also key to Blue Origin's Upcoming Glenn rocket: That heavy lifter features seven or nine BE-4s in its first stage, depending on the configuration. (New Glenn has its own challenges at the moment; it exploded during a test on May 28, and Blue Origin is working to return the powerful rocket to flight.).

Industry observers note that ULA had already noted that Vulcan's six solid rocket boosters (SRBs) and its Centaur V upper stage — which employs a different engine, the RL-10 — seem to perform well on Sunday. Further analysis is firming up that conclusion, according to today's patch.

In a recent development, vulcan has had complications with its SRBs in the past. On the rocket's second and fourth flights — which launched in October 2024 and February of this year, respectively — an SRB nozzle burned through and fell off about 30 seconds into flight. On both occasions, Vulcan overcame the problem and successfully delivered its payload to orbit.

In the wake of the February flight, ULA and Northrop Grumman, which builds the SRBs, tweaked the nozzle design — a fix that apparently worked, based on Sunday's nominal performance.

Sunday's launch was the fifth ever for the two-stage Vulcan Centaur, the successor to ULA's workhorse Atlas V rocket. Vulcan debuted in January 2024 and has now experienced issues on three of its five flights, though Sunday's was the only one that ended in failure.

In a recent development, vulcan was out of action for about nine months after the February SRB issue. It's unclear how long its current grounding will last; that depends on what ULA's anomaly investigation, which the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration is overseeing, ends up finding.

Voting is now open for the BBC Men's Footballer of the Year 2026 award, which will be presented at Sports Personality of the Year.

Fans from the UK can vote from the five-player shortlist of Jude Bellingham, Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe, Rodri and Lamine Yamal.

The vote closes on Friday, 27 November at 09:00 GMT.

The winner of the award - fresh for this year - will be presented during the live Sports Personality of the Year show on Sunday, 13 December.

Alex Kay-Jelski, Director of BBC Sport, said: "From the drama and excitement of the men's World Cup to the moments that have captivated fans across the domestic and international game, 2026 has given us so much to celebrate.

"Our inaugural BBC Men's Footballer of the Year award is about recognising the players who have made this year so special, inspired fans and left their mark on the game.

"It's a fantastic shortlist, and I can't wait to see who the public choose as our first-ever winner.".

The shortlist was selected by an expert panel comprising former international players and some of the BBC's most respected football voices, bringing together a wealth of experience and insight from across the game.

The panel included Cesar Azpilicueta (Spain), Scott Brown (Scotland), Olivier Giroud (France), Shay Given (Republic of Ireland), Hassan Kachloul (Morocco), Lucas Leiva (Brazil), Benni McCarthy (South Africa), Alan Shearer, Ellen White (both England) and Ashley Williams (Wales).

Read more on the five contenders and cast your vote below.

In a recent development, sorry, this vote cannot be loaded. In order to vote you need to enable JavaScript in your browser.

Meet the SPOTY Men's Footballer of the Year contenders.

Club: Real Madrid Position: Midfield.

Bellingham made history this summer as he became the first Englishman to score as many as seven goals at a major tournament.

In a superb World Cup for the midfielder, he memorably netted twice in back-to-back games to help the Three Lions beat Mexico and Norway.

That meant he joined exalted firm as the first player to score two or more goals in successive World Cup knockout games since Diego Maradona in 1986, and the second youngest in history behind Pele in 1958.

Bellingham also became the youngest European player to make an appearance at four different major tournaments, and also reached the milestone of 50 caps at a younger age than any other England men's player.

The goals continued to flow for Real Madrid, too, with Bellingham notching his 50th for the club to move above the legendary Zinedine Zidane in the Los Blancos' all-time scoring charts.

Bellingham was recently joined in the England squad by his brother Jobe.

Club: Bayern Munich Position: Forward.

In a stunning year of goalscoring, Kane become the first Englishman for 25 years (and only fifth in history) to win the Ballon d'Or - awarded to the world's best footballer.

His tally of 73 goals in 65 matches for club and country during a stellar 2025-26 season has only been surpassed in one of Europe's top five leagues by Lionel Messi's 82 for Barcelona and Argentina in 2011-12.

Kane scored 61 of those goals in just 51 appearances for Bayern Munich as he helped the Bavarians to a league and cup double. His total was 19 more than any other player in Europe's top five divisions.

Already England's record goalscorer, he surpassed Peter Shilton's mark of 125 appearances to become the most-capped Englishman in history.

Six goals at this summer's World Cup also helped him overtake Gary Lineker as the Three Lions' record scorer at the tournament, while he joined David Beckham as the only Englishmen to score in three separate World Cups.

Kane scored his first England goal 79 seconds into his debut in 2015.

Club: Real Madrid Position: Forward.

Mbappe came out on top of an enthralling tussle with Lionel Messi at the 2026 World Cup to become the leading goalscorer in the tournament's history.

The France forward, who is still only 27, took his tally to 22 from just three World Cups to finish one ahead of the great Argentine.

Mbappe's 10 goals from eight games this summer meant he won his second World Cup Golden Boot - a feat no player has managed before.

It also made him the first man to reach double figures at a World Cup since Gerd Muller in 1970, with only Just Fontaine (13) and Sandor Kocsis (11) having scored more goals in a single tournament.

Other achievements in a standout year included him finishing runner-up in the Ballon d'Or awards and overtaking Olivier Giroud as France's all-time leading goalscorer.

He scored 25 times to retain his title as La Liga's top scorer during a 2025-26 campaign in which he netted 42 goals in all competitions for Real Madrid.

Mbappe has won eight consecutive league golden boots.

Club: Barcelona Position: Midfield.

Midfield maestro Rodri earned yet another accolade in his incredible career when he was awarded the Golden Ball trophy for the World Cup's best player.

By captaining Spain to glory in the US, Rodri became only the fourth male player to win the World Cup, European Championship, Champions League and Ballon d'Or - following in the footsteps of legendary Germans Gerd Muller and Franz Beckenbauer and France's Zinedine Zidane.

His achievements were made all the more special given doubts remained over whether he would recapture his best form after a long recovery from a serious knee injury in 2024.

Then Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola predicted he would return to his best at the World Cup and he was right. Rodri completed 756 passes there - the most in the tournament since records began in 1966.

His final season at Manchester City before departing for Barcelona ended in familiar fashion with a domestic cup double taking his trophy haul with the club to 14.

Rodri scored the goal that won Manchester City the Champions League in 2023.

Club: Barcelona Position: Forward.

Lamine Yamal continues to rewrite the record books with his astonishing exploits for club and country.

Just days after his 19th birthday, the Spaniard became the youngest footballer to have played in - and won - both a World Cup and a European Championship. The only players younger than him to play in a World Cup final are Brazil's Pele in 1958 and Giuseppe Bergomi for Italy in 1982.

For the second year running, his performances led to a podium place at the Ballon d'Or and at the same award ceremony he became the first footballer in history to win the Young Talent of the Year three years in succession.

Industry observers note that at club level, he was named La Liga's Best Player courtesy of a starring role in Barcelona's title success. The teenager ended the season with an impressive 24 goals and 18 assists across all competitions.

He recently broke Kylian Mbappe's record for the most goals by a teenager in Champions League history.

Lamine Yamal was 16 years and 362 days when he scored at the European Championship in 2024.
